question: The Alpha printing of Magic: the Gathering had a print run of approximately 2.6 million cards. One specific manufacturing detail makes Alpha cards instantly recognizable to collectors — even with white edges hidden. What is that detail?

question: MtG's Color Pie organizes the five colors along a circle: white is opposite black, blue is opposite red, green is opposite black. Each color has two 'enemy' colors and two 'allied' colors. White's allied colors are blue and green. What are white's two enemy colors?

question: MtG's first Pro Tour was held at the Park Central Hotel in New York City in February 1996. It featured 128 invited players competing for a $100,000 prize pool — unprecedented in card games. Who won that first Pro Tour with a White Weenie deck?

question: WrestleMania I on March 31, 1985, at Madison Square Garden featured Hulk Hogan teaming with which celebrity to defeat the team of Roddy Piper and Paul Orndorff?

question: Andre the Giant's iconic confrontation with Hulk Hogan at WrestleMania III took years to build. The two had been on-screen friends until February 7, 1987, when Andre publicly turned on Hogan on the Piper's Pit talk segment. What did Andre famously rip off Hogan's neck?

question: The Ultimate Warrior defeated Hulk Hogan at WrestleMania VI on April 1, 1990, at SkyDome in Toronto, in a champion-vs-champion match. What two titles were unified that night?

choices: WWF Championship and Intercontinental Championship

question: Bret Hart's famous 1992 SummerSlam match against his real-life brother-in-law happened at Wembley Stadium in London. The match drew 80,000+ fans for an Intercontinental Championship bout that the Brit won. Who was Bret's opponent?

question: Mick Foley first won the WWF Championship as Mankind on Raw on January 4, 1999 — a show taped in advance. WCW's Monday Nitro, going head-to-head live, decided to spoil it. Who delivered the spoiler announcement?

question: Stone Cold Steve Austin's first WWF Championship win came at WrestleMania XIV on March 29, 1998, in Boston. He beat Shawn Michaels in Shawn's last match for over four years — Michaels had been suffering from a serious injury. What injury caused Shawn's hiatus?

question: The Rock's catchphrase 'jabronie' — applied to people he considered nobodies — has older wrestling-business roots. question: Kane debuted at the In Your House: Bad Blood pay-per-view on October 5, 1997, interrupting an Undertaker vs Shawn Michaels Hell in a Cell match. The first-ever Hell in a Cell match itself ran 30 minutes, after which the lights went out. Who arrived in a red-and-black costume to attack the Undertaker?

question: Chris Jericho debuted in the WWF on Raw on August 9, 1999, interrupting The Rock with a 30-second countdown that ended in flashing lights. The interruption was the first appearance of which character?

question: Eddie Guerrero's WWF/WWE catchphrase summed up his beloved heel character: he openly admitted he was a cheater. What three-word phrase did Eddie use to embrace this persona?

question: Kurt Angle joined the WWF in late 1999 with a unique credential among professional wrestlers — a real Olympic gold medal. In what discipline did Angle win his gold medal at the 1996 Atlanta Summer Olympics?

question: Steve Largent retired in 1989 holding then-NFL records for receptions, receiving yards, and touchdown receptions. After football, he was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1994 from which state?

question: The Seahawks' offensive line in the mid-2000s was anchored by a Hall-of-Fame left tackle who played his entire 12-year career in Seattle from 1997 to 2008. What was his name?

question: Russell Wilson was a third-round pick (75th overall) in the 2012 NFL Draft. He had transferred for his senior year from one college to another after being passed over as the starter at his original school. Which two schools did he attend in football?

question: Super Bowl XLVIII on February 2, 2014, ended in a 43-8 Seahawks blowout of the Denver Broncos. On the very first play from scrimmage, Manning's snap sailed over his head into the end zone, scoring how for Seattle?

question: Cortez Kennedy spent his entire 11-year career as a defensive tackle with the Seattle Seahawks from 1990 to 2000. He won what major individual NFL honor in 1992, despite the Seahawks finishing 2-14 that season?

question: Ken Griffey Jr's father, Ken Griffey Sr., joined the Mariners for the 1990 season, allowing father and son to play together in the same outfield. On September 14, 1990, they did something no other father-son duo had ever done in a Major League game. What was it?

question: Edgar Martinez's induction into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2019 was a milestone for designated hitters. He was elected in his 10th and final year on the BBWAA ballot. What is the modern best-DH-of-the-year award named?

question: Magic: the Gathering's Power Nine is the most coveted set of cards in the game's history. Eight of the nine were printed only in Alpha, Beta, and Unlimited (1993). question: Richard Garfield's design philosophy for Magic emphasized one principle that has guided MtG design for over thirty years: any combination of three cards in a deck should interact in some meaningful way. Garfield was a longtime board-gamer who eventually designed Roborally, King of Tokyo, and others.

question: Magic: the Gathering's first World Championship in August 1994 at Gen Con in Milwaukee was won by 16-year-old Zak Dolan. The runner-up, Bertrand Lestree from France, was famous for a single deck that has since become legendary in MtG circles. What kind of strategy was Lestree's deck?

question: MtG's June 1994 Legends expansion was the largest set ever printed up to that point — 310 cards. Legends introduced multicolor cards, the legendary supertype, and the 'banding' mechanic. Mana Drain was restricted in Vintage for being a one-cost counterspell that effectively generated free mana.

question: Magic: the Gathering's original 1993 release date is often cited as August 5, 1993, when the first Alpha booster boxes shipped from the printer. question: MtG's June 1994 Legends expansion introduced the Elder Dragon cycle: five legendary three-color dragons that each cost 8 mana. question: The Black Lotus card from MtG Alpha has become a symbol of trading-card value. In 2021, a single PSA Gem Mint 10 Alpha Black Lotus signed by Christopher Rush, the original illustrator, sold at auction for a record-breaking sum. What was the approximate price?

question: Magic: the Gathering's first banned-and-restricted list for tournament play in 1994 named several cards. question: Stone Cold Steve Austin was originally signed to WCW in 1991 as 'Stunning' Steve Austin, where he held the United States Heavyweight Championship and the Television Championship. WCW Vice President Eric Bischoff famously fired him in 1995 with what infamous medium of communication?

question: Mick Foley's 1999 autobiography 'Have a Nice Day: A Tale of Blood and Sweatsocks' was a New York Times bestseller. Foley wrote the entire book longhand in spiral notebooks. question: The Montreal Screwjob on November 9, 1997, at the Molson Centre, came at the Survivor Series in Bret Hart's home country of Canada. question: D-Generation X's signature catchphrase was a question and answer, delivered with crotch-chopping flourishes that became merch gold. Shawn Michaels and Triple H would shout the question; the crowd would shout the answer. What was the call-and-response?

question: The Rock's first WWF Championship reign began at Survivor Series on November 15, 1998. The Rock pinned Mankind in the finals of a 14-man tournament for the vacant WWF title. What controversial development from the match created a key Attitude-Era heel turn?

question: Vince McMahon Jr. inherited control of Capitol Wrestling Corporation from his father in 1982. Under his ownership it became WWF and then WWE. Roddy Piper, from Stampede Wrestling in Calgary
context: Hogan had been working for Verne Gagne's AWA and had developed Hulkamania there. Vince Jr signed him in December 1983 and immediately put the WWF title on him in January 1984. The territorial system collapsed within a few years; Vince had bought the country.

question: Chyna, billed as the Ninth Wonder of the World (Andre the Giant having been the Eighth), broke major gender barriers in the WWF. In 1999, she became the first woman to enter the Royal Rumble, and later that year became the first to win the Intercontinental Championship. question: Eddie Guerrero's nephew Chavo Guerrero, the Dominik Dijakovic moment of Eddie's career came in the same family wrestling tradition. The Guerrero family had a multi-generational wrestling dynasty going back to Eddie's father. Where was the Guerrero family promotion based?

question: Super Bowl XL on February 5, 2006, in Detroit ended in a 21-10 loss for the Seahawks to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The game was marred by officiating controversies. Late in the third quarter, Seattle thought they had taken the lead on a Jerramy Stevens catch ruled in-bounds; head referee Bill Leavy reversed it. context: Leavy made his public apology at Seahawks training camp in 2010. He acknowledged the Darrell Jackson offensive pass interference (waving off a TD) and a holding call on Sean Locklear were both wrong calls. Mike Holmgren said the team felt they had to beat 'two opponents' in the game.

question: Marshawn Lynch's nickname 'Beast Mode' was actually a phrase he picked up at Cal-Berkeley as an undergraduate. His infamous 2015 Super Bowl-week media boycott included a single repeated phrase to every question reporters asked. What was the phrase?
answer: I'm just here so I won't get fined

Thanks for asking, no comment
Beast Mode, that's all I got
context: Lynch had been fined repeatedly by the NFL for refusing to speak to media. At Super Bowl XLIX media day, he attended for less than five minutes and used the line as his only response. The NFL eventually changed media-availability rules after the Lynch saga.

question: The Seahawks-Patriots Super Bowl XLIX ended with one of the most famous play calls in football history. With one yard to go and 26 seconds left, on second down, offensive coordinator Darrell Bevell called a slant pass to Ricardo Lockette instead of a Lynch run. Why did Bevell later say the team didn't run the ball there?
answer: To save time and avoid a third-down clock issue
choices: To save time and avoid a third-down clock issue
Wilson had audibled out of the planned run call
The Patriots had only one timeout left and Seattle panicked
Lynch was injured and needed a play to catch his breath
context: Bevell took heat from fans for the call. Pete Carroll defended it as the best decision given the Patriots' goal-line stack expected a run. Malcolm Butler had been studying that exact play on film all week. The play call is one of the most second-guessed in NFL history.

question: On January 8, 2011, Marshawn Lynch's 67-yard touchdown against the Saints became 'The Beast Quake' because seismographs at the University of Washington detected ground tremors from the crowd reaction. How long after the run did the seismograph spike?
answer: Within about 30 seconds, with continued aftershocks during replays
choices: Within about 30 seconds, with continued aftershocks during replays
Two full minutes later when fans saw the highlight on the JumboTron
About 5 seconds after Lynch broke the eighth tackle
The recording was actually triggered by the half-time fireworks
context: The University of Washington's Pacific Northwest Seismic Network operates a station near Magnuson Park about 2 miles from CenturyLink Field. The detected magnitude was about 1.0-2.0, technically too small to be considered a real earthquake. The Beast Quake II during the 2013 playoffs against the Saints (also a Lynch TD) was even bigger.

question: Pete Carroll arrived in Seattle in 2010 after winning two BCS National Championships at USC in 2003 and 2004. The Seahawks' previous coach had been fired after a 5-11 season. Who was Pete Carroll's immediate predecessor as head coach in Seattle?
answer: Jim Mora Jr., who lasted only one season as head coach

context: Jim Mora Jr was Mike Holmgren's defensive backs coach who was promoted before Carroll arrived. He coached just the 2009 season (5-11). Holmgren left in 2008 after a decade. Carroll became GM and head coach, building the Legion of Boom defense from the ground up.

question: On October 8, 1995, in Game 5 of the ALDS, Edgar Martinez's series-winning double in the 11th inning scored Joey Cora from third and Ken Griffey Jr. from first base. Dave Niehaus's radio call has become a Mariners legend. What words did Niehaus famously shout as Griffey scored?
answer: 'My oh my!' and 'The Mariners are going to play for the American League Championship!'

'Goodness gracious!' and 'Griffey scores and Seattle wins it all!'
context: Niehaus's full call: 'Right now the Mariners are going to play for the American League Championship! I don't believe it! It just continues! My oh my!' The call has been played thousands of times at Safeco Field. Niehaus was inducted into the Hall of Fame broadcaster wing in 2008. He died in November 2010 of a heart attack.

question: Ken Griffey Jr.'s 2016 Hall of Fame election set a then-record for highest vote percentage in any Cooperstown class. His vote was unanimous-but-three-short — three writers did not vote for him for various reasons. What was his exact percentage?
answer: 99.3% (437 out of 440 ballots)

97.5% (429 out of 440 ballots)
context: Griffey's 99.3% topped Tom Seaver's previous record of 98.84%. The record stood until Mariano Rivera became the first unanimous Hall-of-Famer in 2019. Derek Jeter then missed unanimity by one vote in 2020 (99.7%). The three writers who did not vote for Griffey never revealed themselves publicly.

question: Randy Johnson came to the Seattle Mariners in 1989 via a trade from the Montreal Expos. Seattle's GM Woody Woodward sent which young pitcher to Montreal to acquire Johnson?
answer: Mark Langston, the Mariners' previous lefty ace
choices: Mark Langston, the Mariners' previous lefty ace

context: The Langston-for-Johnson trade is regarded as one of the most lopsided in baseball history in Seattle's favor. Johnson went on to win four Cy Youngs (the first in 1995). Langston had a solid career but never matched Johnson's dominance. The Mariners also got Brian Holman and Gene Harris in the deal.

question: Ichiro Suzuki's career hit total combining Japan and the United States is widely cited as a global baseball record. What is the approximate combined total?
answer: 4,367 hits combined — 1,278 in Japan and 3,089 in the United States

context: Ichiro reached 4,257 hits in 2016 (passing Pete Rose's MLB record) and continued through the end of his Marlins career. Pete Rose still claims the official MLB record because Ichiro's Japanese hits don't count toward MLB stats. The 4,367 total is commemorated by displays in Cooperstown and at the Orix Buffaloes museum.

question: On August 15, 2012, Felix Hernandez threw a perfect game against the Tampa Bay Rays at Safeco Field — 27 batters up, 27 down. It was the 23rd perfect game in MLB history and the third in 2012 alone. Which other two pitchers threw perfect games that 2012 season?
answer: Philip Humber and Matt Cain

Mariano Rivera and Roy Halladay
Justin Verlander and Cliff Lee

context: Philip Humber's perfecto came April 21 vs the Mariners; Cain's was June 13 vs Houston. Hernandez's came August 15. Three perfect games in one season is unprecedented. King Felix struck out 12; he became the first AL pitcher to throw a perfecto since David Cone in 1999.

question: MtG's 1993 Beta set was meant to fix Alpha's print errors and reprint the same cards. But a single dual land that had appeared in Alpha was omitted from Beta — apparently due to a print-sheet mistake. It was not reprinted until Revised in April 1994. The omission made the Beta version of this dual land effectively nonexistent, and the Alpha version highly prized. What was the missing dual land?
answer: Volcanic Island, the red-blue dual land
choices: Volcanic Island, the red-blue dual land
Plateau, the red-white dual land
Underground Sea, the blue-black dual land
Bayou, the black-green dual land
context: Volcanic Island and Circle of Protection: Black were both omitted from Beta. Alpha Volcanic Islands command extreme collector premiums for this reason. The dual lands joined the Reserved List in 1996, so the Alpha printing remains the rarest. Garfield himself credited the duals as the most important non-Power Nine cards for shaping competitive MtG.

question: MtG's Antiquities expansion in March 1994 introduced the Urza-Mishra Brothers' War storyline. The set included a specific land card that became infamous in tournament Magic for enabling rapid mana acceleration through artifact creature spam. The card was Mishra's Workshop, which produces three colorless mana — but only to cast artifact spells. The card was originally printed at uncommon and never reprinted in the same form. What single specific reprint of Antiquities cards happened, and which year, that excluded Mishra's Workshop?
answer: Chronicles in 1995, which reprinted other Antiquities cards but skipped Mishra's Workshop

Battle Royale in 1999, which used Antiquities cards in pre-built decks
context: Chronicles reprinted Atlantic-Nights through The Dark in white-bordered form. Mishra's Workshop was deliberately omitted because Wizards recognized its tournament power. It joined the Reserved List in 1996 and has never been reprinted in any product. Alpha-Beta-Unlimited (1993) Workshops still command thousands of dollars; the Antiquities printing is the only one.

question: MtG's Legends expansion in June 1994 introduced the Elder Dragon cycle: five legendary three-color dragons, including Nicol Bolas (blue-black-red) and Arcades Sabboth (white-blue-green). Each cost 8 mana to cast. They had a notorious design quirk that made them hard to keep on the table despite their power level. What was that quirk?
answer: Each upkeep, you paid 3 mana of their colors or sacrificed them

Each turn, you skipped your draw step or sacrificed two lands
Each combat, you attacked with them or paid 5 generic mana
context: The upkeep tax of three colored mana made the Elder Dragons unplayable in any deck that wasn't full of mana fixing — by design. The 'must attack' clause was a separate flavor rule on some printings. Their design legacy is enormous: the Elder Dragon Highlander format (later renamed Commander) takes its name from this cycle.

question: MtG's first Pro Tour in February 1996 at the Park Central Hotel in New York City had a $100,000 prize pool — unprecedented for any card game at the time. The 128-player event was won by Michael Loconto. Wizards of the Coast deliberately chose the format to make competitive Magic accessible to players who didn't own the Power Nine. What did that mean for which cards were legal?
answer: The Power Nine and other Alpha-Beta-Unlimited rarities were excluded

Only cards printed in the previous twelve months were eligible
All cards from every printed set were legal, including reserved list
Only cards in current print runs as of January 1996 were allowed
context: The 1996 format limited cards to recent printings — Fourth Edition base set and the most recent expansions. The exclusion of the Power Nine meant decks could not be dominated by Alpha rarities. Loconto won $12,000 with a white aggressive creature deck. The Pro Tour later evolved into a circuit of multiple events per year, including the World Championship.

question: MtG's Reserved List was created in 1996 in response to fan anger over reprints in the 1995 Chronicles set. The Reserved List initially contained over 500 cards. In 2002, Wizards modified the list, removing one specific category of card while leaving the rares intact. What category did they remove from the Reserved List in 2002?
answer: Uncommons and commons from Antiquities, Arabian Nights, Legends, and The Dark
choices: Uncommons and commons from Antiquities, Arabian Nights, Legends, and The Dark

All five basic-land variants printed only in early black-bordered sets
context: The 2002 change angered some collectors but allowed reprints of cards like Hymn to Tourach and Land Tax. The Reserved List today contains 569 rare cards and a handful of uncommons that were grandfathered in. Wizards has firmly committed to never modifying the Reserved List again — most recently confirmed in 2010 and 2017.

question: Magic: the Gathering's classic artwork has its own collector subculture. The Alpha card Black Lotus was illustrated by Christopher Rush, the same artist who illustrated Mox Pearl and many other iconic Alpha cards. Rush's distinctive style influenced MtG's visual identity. Rush died in 2016, but had spent his final years signing Alpha cards at MtG conventions. What did fans nickname these specific signed cards?
answer: Rush Lotuses, with PSA Mint 10 signed copies commanding particular value at auction

context: Christopher Rush's signed Black Lotuses sell for premiums of $50,000-$200,000+ over unsigned copies. The PSA-graded auction in January 2021 of a signed PSA 10 Alpha Lotus reached $511,000. Rush also illustrated Mox Pearl, Mox Jet, Sengir Vampire, Hypnotic Specter, and Sword of the Ages, among other iconic Alpha cards.

question: MtG's first official novel was published in 1994 — a companion piece for the Arabian Nights expansion. The novel was written by Jeff Grubb and centered on the planeswalker Taysir of Rabiah. The line ended with the Acclaim Comics bankruptcy in 1997. The early novels and comics were the foundation of the MtG storyline before the late-90s revival under Wizards' in-house creative team.

question: Among the rare cards in MtG's June 1994 Legends expansion, one legendary land is consistently considered the most expensive — it makes each creature's controller pay one mana per upkeep or sacrifice them. Played copies command thousands of dollars. What is the card?
answer: The Tabernacle at Pendrell Vale, a legendary land

question: MtG's 1993 Alpha set was printed on three large uncut press sheets, each containing 121 cards in an 11-by-11 grid. The print sheet positioning created a peculiar effect: certain rares appear at slightly different rates than others, because the print runs for the three sheets weren't identical. Among Alpha's rares, Black Lotus and the five Moxes are the most legendary — but a single Alpha rare is statistically rarer than the others because of a specific print-sheet quirk. answer: Volcanic Island, which appeared only on certain print runs

Bayou, which was double-printed on the uncommon sheet
context: Volcanic Island was famously missing from the Beta set due to a printing error and not reprinted until Revised in April 1994. Alpha Volcanic Islands command extreme premiums on the collector market — well above the other dual lands. The other dual lands (Bayou, Tundra, Underground Sea, Tropical Island, etc.) all appeared in both Alpha and Beta. The dual lands joined the Reserved List in 1996.

question: Stone Cold Steve Austin's signature 'Austin 3:16' line — delivered after his King of the Ring 1996 win — came together in an unusual way. The original 3:16 shirt is now a wrestling-merchandise collector's item. Sales peaked in 1998 at over 1 million Austin shirts moved.

question: Mick Foley's first WWF Championship win on January 4, 1999, on a taped Raw episode was an Attitude-Era pivot — but also a turning point in the Monday Night Wars. Tony Schiavone's now-infamous WCW Nitro spoiler announcement reportedly drove ~600,000 viewers to flip from Nitro to Raw mid-show. He had been pressured by Ted Turner to attack Vince McMahon directly on-air
He thought the spoiler would draw a lawsuit that would publicize WCW Nitro
context: Bischoff's miscalculation is one of the most-quoted strategic errors in the Monday Night Wars. The flip-over moment is often cited as the night WWF won the war for good. Schiavone later said he had no choice — the spoiler was Bischoff's call. He has expressed regret in multiple later interviews.

question: The Montreal Screwjob on November 9, 1997, was filmed for what became the documentary 'Wrestling with Shadows.' The documentarian Paul Jay was given unprecedented access to Bret Hart in the months leading up to the event. After the screwjob, Bret Hart famously confronted Vince McMahon backstage and connected a punch. The documentary shows the moments leading up to and after the screwjob in real time. Bret breaking out of the Sharpshooter and punching Michaels in the face
context: The 'WCW' fingers-in-the-air moment came after the bell rang. Bret had figured out the screwjob was happening only moments before the bell. Wrestling with Shadows captures the locker-room aftermath including Bret's punch on McMahon. The film won the Special Jury Prize at the 1998 Hot Docs Festival.

question: The first Hell in a Cell match in October 1997 between The Undertaker and Shawn Michaels at the Bad Blood pay-per-view featured a memorable storyline conclusion: the lights went out and Kane debuted to attack Undertaker. The very next Hell in a Cell, June 28, 1998 (King of the Ring), produced wrestling's most infamous bumps when Mick Foley as Mankind was thrown off the cell. context: Foley's tooth went through his upper lip and stuck out of his nose. He continued the match — including being thrown into thumbtacks. Vince McMahon famously yelled, 'Will somebody stop the damn match?' on commentary. The bumps are widely considered the two most dangerous spots in wrestling history.

question: The nWo formation at Bash at the Beach 1996 was a months-long buildup. Eric Bischoff brought in former WWF stars Scott Hall and Kevin Nash to pretend they were attacking WCW from outside the company. The reveal that Hulk Hogan was the 'third man' came on July 7, 1996. context: WWF sued WCW in summer 1996 over the visual presentation of Scott Hall as 'the Bad Guy' (directly evoking his Razor Ramon character) and Kevin Nash as the WWF-style 'Big Sexy' (his Diesel persona). The case settled with WCW agreeing to certain disclaimers. The disputes are detailed in 'The Death of WCW' by R.D. Reynolds and Bryan Alvarez.

question: The Rock vs Stone Cold WrestleMania X-Seven main event on April 1, 2001, at the Astrodome in Houston is often called the greatest main event in WrestleMania history. The match featured Vince McMahon's interference — Austin's heel turn was the swerve of the night. The exact ending played out with Austin hitting The Rock with a Stunner, McMahon handing Austin chairs, and Austin pinning The Rock. answer: Toasted Vince McMahon with two beer cans on the ring apron as the show went off the air

Sprayed beer on The Rock's prone body in the center of the ring
Lifted McMahon onto his shoulders as the ramp's pyrotechnics went off
Shared a fist-bump with McMahon as the camera zoomed in
context: The Austin-McMahon beer toast was the visual confirmation of the heel turn. Austin was scripted to wink at the camera and toast Vince as a new alliance forming. The match's WWE Network rating remains exceptionally high among historic matches. Austin's heel run that followed was widely criticized as creatively disappointing, but the WrestleMania match itself stands as a five-star classic.

question: WrestleMania X8 on March 17, 2002, at Toronto's SkyDome marked the official end of WCW as separate competition; Vince McMahon had purchased WCW in March 2001. The main event was Hogan vs The Rock — Icon vs Icon. Hogan was scripted as the heel; the Toronto crowd ignored the script and cheered Hogan throughout. answer: The Rock and Hogan called audibles to swap multiple key spots so Hogan could absorb the crowd's love as he faced his exit

The Rock walked out of the match mid-stride, demanding a script revision before continuing
Hogan tore up the rest of the script and ad-libbed his entire remaining offense

Hogan's post-match handshake with The Rock and 'do the right thing' gesture mid-fight created an organic face turn for Hogan. He went on to win his sixth WWF Championship a few weeks later at Backlash 2002.

question: Triple H's Pedigree finisher — the double-arm underhook into a face-first drop — was developed by Paul Levesque as his signature move in the WWF in 1995. The move's name nods to a specific elite-society or aristocratic concept. Considering Hunter Hearst Helmsley's snobby blue-blooded character at the time, what did 'pedigree' originally refer to?

Levesque adapted the basic move concept from earlier wrestlers but made it his signature. The character softened into D-Generation X's degenerate version in 1997.

question: ECW's hardcore match format involving barbed wire, light tubes, and exploding rings derived directly from Japanese deathmatch wrestling. Paul Heyman imported Japanese hardcore wrestlers to ECW shows in Philadelphia. Which Japanese wrestler founded FMW in 1989 — the company that pioneered the deathmatch genre — and later appeared in ECW?
answer: Atsushi Onita

Mitsuharu Misawa
Genichiro Tenryu
Tarzan Goto
context: Atsushi Onita founded FMW (Frontier Martial-Arts Wrestling) in 1989. His no-rope barbed-wire and exploding-ring matches stunned audiences. Sabu, Terry Funk, and other ECW stars regularly worked Japanese deathmatch tours. Onita's influence on Heyman's Philadelphia hardcore booking is well documented in the wrestling press.

question: The Undertaker's WrestleMania streak began at WrestleMania VII in 1991 against Jimmy Snuka and ran 21-0 until broken at WrestleMania XXX on April 6, 2014, by Brock Lesnar. Multiple opponents got tantalizingly close to ending the streak. Which 2009 WrestleMania match against Shawn Michaels is widely cited as the closest call?
answer: WrestleMania XXV, a match that won the year's pro-wrestling Match of the Year awards

WrestleMania XXIX, a no-holds-barred stipulation that Shawn won by reversal
context: Shawn Michaels vs Undertaker at WrestleMania XXV (April 2009) is widely considered one of the greatest WrestleMania matches in history. Both performers kicked out at the absolute last instant on multiple near-falls. Brock Lesnar broke the streak 21-1 at WrestleMania XXX with three F-5s. The 21-1 final score is the canonical reference.

question: The Iron Sheik — Khosrow Vaziri — dropped the WWF Championship to Hulk Hogan on January 23, 1984, kicking off Hulkamania. Sheik had won the title from Bob Backlund a month earlier. The original plan, according to multiple later accounts, had been for someone else to be Hogan's first championship victim — and a major WWF deal in late 1983 was specifically structured so Sheik would 'job out' to Hogan. Who was the originally-planned opponent that the WWF replaced with the Iron Sheik?

Sgt. Slaughter, whose return from AWA was delayed
Big John Studd, who had a clause that prevented him losing on his Garden debut

context: The booking has been speculated about for years; multiple accounts (including books like 'Sheik' by Page Magen and various Hogan interviews) suggest Bob Backlund's title transition to Hogan was complex and that the Sheik was selected because he could be relied on to do the job correctly. Backlund himself had been a long-running champion (1978-1983) but the WWF wanted a 'foreign menace' transitional champion before the Hogan victory.

question: Super Bowl XLIX on February 1, 2015, ended with one of the most-replayed plays in NFL history: the Malcolm Butler interception of Russell Wilson at the goal line. Butler had been an undrafted rookie out of West Alabama; he had been studying the exact play formation on film for the entire week before the game. The specific play call that the Patriots had repeatedly drilled against was 'PIC' (or 'Goal Line, Slant').
